I thought The Operator would be like Papers, Please, with a strong gameplay loop. However, it’s purely a narrative-driven game where all mechanisms are subsumed under the plot arc. 

The lore isn’t developed enough, and the duration is artificially inflated by excessive filler, which feels unnecessary given the game’s 2-hour length.

I'm only giving this a thumbs down because I believe this is marketed incorrectly. I loved the game for what it is, a visual novel. But this is not necessarily a detective game, and I'd argue not even really investigative.
The game follows one story line, and kind of fools you into thinking your choices matter when they really don't. For example, I attempted every dialogue option to not work with HAL, but that didn't matter, I had to work with them anyway.
The tools used are awesome; facial recognition, Human Database, lab analysis. But we only use some of these things once or a few times at most.
Don't get me wrong, the story is fantastic, and I genuinely loved my time with it. I agree with a lot of the other reviews that this should be way longer, but overall, I think the game is marketed incorrectly which is where I can't recommend it. I, and it seems a lot of others, went into this with the idea I would be solving multiple cases, using the technology multiple times, maybe even an endless mode where there's multiple variations of possible cases. 
I do think it's a great game, the immersion into the FDI computer is fantastic, the art style/graphics are perfect, everything ran smoothly. I mean genuinely top marks across (most of) the board. But it did leave me wanting more, I really dislike that we only used some of the tools once, and my choices didn't matter. All that being said, I absolutely would purchase another game from this dev.
It's a short game, but it's cheap. The story and voiceover are really good. Kudos for trying something "different" with the ending. Looking forward for his next project.

This game has an interesting premise and it has been made well. The graphics are good and the audio is top notch in my books.

But unfortunately it's... hmm, how should I say it... easy? Or not even that, hand-heldy! Like, it doesn't really let you do much anything of worth outside of one high stakes scene that is timed. But that it not what 99% of the game is.

It's kinda like this game is backwards from what you would expect from a logic puzzle game. It's the Agents or other people that call you aka the NPC's aka the game itself that do most of the detective work. And you, the player, are the computer whose job is to do the tedious work of checking. You get one single question to answer from the field agent and the answer is never that hard to find. In fact it's almost never necessary to collect and compile information as an active researcher and there's basically no need to take notes. Most of the times you just click on the right, kinda obvious document and do the thing and then answer so the plot may thiccen.

And it's not like the setting of the game, you being the computer guy helping detectives in the field means it has to be boring. There could have been more you could do. But most of the intrigue in this game comes from chat interactions, not from actual action you get to do.

Like for example, there are two things that could have been so fun to get to use as active participant, as part of a larger puzzle YOU need to solve yourself, the chemical analysis software and the bomb defusing manual, that only get one use. And also, no love for the vehicle database, just for people database. But like, just being able to do more than to just find out an answer to one question at a time, being able to take notes and to make actual deductions? Would have been fun. Think of Mainlining as an example.

It's just that, there is so much promise. This game was instant purchase for me as soon as I found out about it, as a fan of mystery and "hacking" genre of games. But it just didn't really deliver what I hoped for. And I'm kinda bummed about it.

This game only has one ending, and only less than 2½ - 3 hours of content in total, making the cost per played hour very high. 
The one singular ending is quite bad, and even though there are many dialogue options, there are no actual meaningful choices to be made.
There are numerous quite long and somewhat boring unskippable cut scenes. However one could argue that having no skip option is acceptable due to it being somewhat important to pay attention to the them. And since there's only one ending, there's no replayability, and so there's no need to have a skip option. Though realistically, and as others have pointed out, the most probable reason for not having a skip option is to extend the required playtime to over 2 hours so the game cannot be refunded through Steam.
The game has a lot of dialogue, and not a lot of gameplay. What little actual gameplay there is, is enjoyable enough I guess, but also pretty simplistic and easy. This can be seen as both a positive and a negative. If you're looking for any sort of a challenge/puzzle, you will not find it in this game. This game should be definitely thought of as a visual novel more than a puzzle game.
The story itself is mediocre and actually pretty shallow, which is very bad for a game that consists mainly of the story.
The dialogue is fully voice-acted (except for [spoiler]HAL[/spoiler] and the protagonist), which is a definite plus. The voice acting is also pretty high-quality. However I cannot help but feel like way too much developer effort and money was put into the voice acting, when it should've been put into other aspects of the game.
The soundscape and the soundtrack are also good, but really nothing out of the ordinary.

Overall, The Operator is a short, pricey mediocre dialogue-heavy and minimal-gameplay game with high-quality voice acting and heavy hand-holding and railroading, and with only one ending. It feels like the game was designed to be just long enough to make it impossible to refund after reaching the ending (which in fairness one shouldn't do regardless, if they enjoyed the game and reached the ending).

I cannot recommend anything else but to watch someone else such as a YouTuber play this game. I think that will actually add way more to the experience than buying the game and playing it on your own.

Very positive experience. Yes, it's a very "on the rails" linear story. However, it allows your imagination to run wild and feel like you are in a movie. I really dug the puzzles. If you spend some time with the files and mechanics, you might discover some things before they are part of the story, but that's okay, it makes you feel really smart! 

Would it be cool if there were some branching story lines with different endings or character development as you choose different dialogue choices? Sure. But it doesn't take away from the overall experience. And I think it was really fun. It was reminding me a little of "Majestic" from the early 00s. Does anyone remember that game/experience? 

Overall, if you like linear story-telling, feeling like a boss detective, this is a fun 5-hour game. I definitely had some nail-biting moments in it. Great job, devs! Look forward to more!

Great Concept, the puzzle (the few) were great. The bomb defusing manual idea, fantastic, and I dont know if it was my computer settings or the game that had the manuals letters hard to focus on.. But it is short, and feels like it only takes longer to finish because of the transition "scenes" if you could call them that. I am assuming it is by design? Because the return policy of steam, if you play under a certain amount of minutes you can ask for a refund? Who knows. - Mean but Brilliant.

I truly did love the concept, the idea, the story is great. I finished it in 4 hours, and it would have been less, if I didnt accidentally have the bomb blow up (twice) and the "transition scenes" weren't so annoying long.

The ending, unsatisfying. And I am assuming it is a loading screen where you hear the character breathing, walking, swallowing (yuk) etc. but its all just colours smooshing around on the screen. It cant be skipped either. If there was a loading bar, or something to actually keep my interest it might have been okay.

If there is no sequel, it would have been nice to have alternate endings? or something that was a result of your decisions. 

Another thing I would have liked to see was save points, though I guess because the ending was to be essentially the same maybe it didnt matter? If the bomb went off would the ending have been different or would I have had to start that section again anyway ( I kept closing and opening the game as soon as the bomb went off because I wanted to try again. I dont know if it would have made me try again or not for the story, I may or may not explore this game further.

If there is a sequel (and it was designed like this) I would have been nice to let us know we are only buying a chapter, I would have reconsidered paying the amount that I did. I will still probably want to play another chapter, because it is like a story that I want to know the ending, but I will be waiting for it to go on sale.

Enhance! It's a short, immersive, detective game, best played with headphones on for the music. While sometimes the music is a bit too intrusive, it's very good, especially the ending (keep watching all the way through). The DOS based menus are exactly like they used to be in the nineties, even if there were no cell phones then, so I would guess that liberties were taken and we are in an alternative universe.

It's hard to give a GOOD or BAD opinion on this game. The visuals and astounding, music is perfect, voice acting is awesome. I love that you access FDI's system so it feels pretty real. Good things aside, the storyline is linear. Only after checking the forum I found out that your choices, hm... don't really matter. I feel like the game could use some filler cases to solve, rather than make the player wait for anyone to contact them regarding the main case. The case itself was pretty interesting and it's good to wait for the end credits, some cool stuff is shown there ;)

Overall, I enjoyed the game a lot but I can't shake the feeling it should be cheaper given what it offers right now. Maybe the developers will make some DLC? That would be awesome.

I definitely recommend playing with headphones and no background noise. And there's a fun, exciting twist at the end that got my heart pounding. I highly recommend this one, especially if you enjoyed games like Orwell and Need to Know.
